status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026, checked by the translation workers, and deployed to earthfluent.com on 13 November 2026. Brazilian Portuguese, as the course is: ônibus, cachorro, você.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Nasal Sounds, Part 1
lessons.description: A tilde sends the vowel through the nose. Hear it in pão, mãe, não, and irmã.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Nh and Lh, Part 1
lessons.description: Nh sounds like the ny in canyon, and lh like the lli in million. Hear vinho, amanhã, filho, and trabalho.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Letter Ç, Part 1
lessons.description: A ç is always a soft s and never a k. Hear it in açúcar, coração, cabeça, and almoço.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Accent Marks, Part 1
lessons.description: An accent mark can be the only thing that tells two words apart. Compare e with é, and avó with avô.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb ir, to go, changes to say who is going. Spot what changes, and what você and ela share: vou, vai, vai, vamos.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of ir, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are about to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: For more than one, the word gains an s, and so does its "the": o becomes os, and a becomes as.

lessons.title: Patterns - Words That Match, Part 1
lessons.description: A describing word matches the thing it describes: vermelho with o carro, vermelha with a casa. Spot the ending that changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: A Portuguese question usually has the same words in the same order as the statement. Only the voice rises.
words: This is the bus to São Paulo.
Este é o ônibus para São Paulo.
Is this the bus to São Paulo?
Este é o ônibus para São Paulo?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: To say something is not so, put não in front of the verb. Nothing else in the sentence changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come After, Part 1
lessons.description: In English the describing word comes first: a white house. In Portuguese it usually comes after: uma casa branca.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Two Words for Is, Part 1
lessons.description: Portuguese has two words for is: é for what something is like by nature, and está for how it is right now.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb ir, to go, at work in whole sentences. Spot vou, vamos, vai, and vão.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. Spot what the answer keeps from the question, and what it changes.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: Describing words matching what they describe, in whole sentences: branca, vermelhos, alta, pequenos.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways: already done, happening now, and still to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
